answer: Agents must submit a zero-knowledge proof that their assigned private model checkpoint was generated inside one of a fixed orchard of TEE enclaves whose firmware is bound to a physical unclonable function with a unique pigment speckle pattern; the enclave signs one long-lived identity per chip. A sybil attacker cannot clone that PUF, so at the market nadir for secure microcontrollers each fake identity costs about $0.85 for a new chip plus enrollment gas, making mass sybil linear in hardware cost.
